Population increased in Southwark

The estimated population of Southwark in 2024 was 314,786 usual residents, a rise of 0.4% since 2023.

This meant that Southwark's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Southwark increased by 2.6%.

Over this slightly longer period, Southwark was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Southwark

The average (median) age rose to 33.6 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Southwark has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Southwark is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Southwark's population of 314,786 usual residents was made up of:

  • 49,020 people aged 0 to 15 years, (15.6%)
  • 237,084 people aged 16 to 64 years, (75.3%)
  • 28,682 people aged 65 years and over, (9.1%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Southwark has a higher proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (75.3% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Southwark, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Southwark
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Southwark, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 1,857 people (0.6%). In total, there were 3,224 births and 1,367 deaths in Southwark.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 6,040 (-1.9%). There were 35,190 people entering the area and 41,230 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Southwark's population of 5,488 (1.8%) as a result of 12,353 people entering the area and 6,865 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Southwark was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Southwark in mid-2023 is 313,485.

Within this, international migration was revised downwards by 1,439 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 595 people.

Overall, there was an revision downwards of 2,034 people.
